A subterranean barracks-hall, row upon row of iron-framed bunks receding under a low vaulted ceiling, the silence of ten thousand sleeping soldiers heavy in the stone dark.
A great aqueduct-hall, stone channels carrying underground rivers in tiered cascades across a cavern wide enough to swallow a town, the roar of water filling every inch of air.
A vast mushroom-forest cavern, enormous fungi rising forty feet from the cave floor, their pale caps glowing faintly, the dark between their stalks absolute and very deep.
A colosseum-vast fighting-pit ringed by tiered stone seats carved from the cavern walls, the floor of packed granite far below, the upper galleries lost in torch-smoke and shadow.
A grand ceremonial bath-hall, pools of geothermal water steaming in a cavern of carved pillars and mosaic floors, the vaulted ceiling sweating warm condensation in the golden light.
A deep ore-processing hall, iron ore tipping down massive stone chutes into sorting floors below, the grinding roar of stone machinery filling a cavern three hundred feet across.
A hall of ancestor-masks, every inch of the vast curved walls hung with iron death-masks of the dwarven dead, their empty eyes staring across the torchlit gulf below.
A subterranean observatory-vault, a great shaft bored upward through a mile of mountain, the single pinhole of sky above visible as a pale star from the dark floor.
A vast armory-hall, weapons racked from floor to ceiling along walls that stretch away into darkness, the iron smell overwhelming, the scale of prepared war staggering and cold.
A deep crystal-cavern throne-room, walls and ceiling thick with natural quartz formations glittering in torchlight, the dwarven throne at the center dwarfed by the raw geological splendor around it.
A great smelting-cavern, rivers of molten iron running in stone troughs across a floor wide as a battlefield, the sky of the ceiling hidden behind permanent iron-smoke and heat.
A collapsed outer hall open to the mountain itself, one wall sheared away by ancient catastrophe, the cavern now yawning onto a sheer cliff-face and the vast cold dark beyond.

A colossal pillared throne-hall carved from living black granite, its vaulted ceiling lost three hundred feet above in torch-smoke and shadow, row upon row of rune-stamped columns marching into the gloom beyond sight.

A vast forge-cavern threaded by molten lava channels, great stone furnaces the size of towers roaring along both walls, the hammering of unseen smiths echoing across an immensity of scorched and glowing rock.

A deep mine-shaft plunging into glowing darkness far below, tier upon tier of carved stone galleries spiraling down its walls, the distant bottom lost in amber phosphorescent murk a thousand feet beneath.

A grand processional hall lined with colossal dwarf-king statues, each hewn a hundred feet tall from the living mountain, their bearded faces stern above guttering braziers, receding in perfect symmetry into crushing dark.

A great underground market-cavern the size of a buried city, its vaulted ceiling crusted with carved stalactites, a thousand stone stalls crowding a floor worn smooth by uncounted centuries of dwarven boots.
